transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. My wife and adult son really pushed for me to come in because they say I've been acting all over the place at work and at home lately. It feels like I can't quite control what I'm doing or keep my actions appropriate to what is actually going on around me.
Do you feel like you are hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, or do you have any unusual beliefs that others might find hard to understand?

No, I don't hear any voices or see things that aren't there, and I don't think I have any strange beliefs. It's really more about how my thoughts get so jumbled up and how hard it is to control my physical actions.
Have you ever had a head injury, a stroke, or any other significant medical condition that affected your brain before these behavioral changes started?

No, I've never had any head injuries, a stroke, or any other medical conditions affecting my brain before all of this. My health has actually been pretty good up until these changes started happening.

During these episodes where you feel out of control, have you ever felt that you were so powerful, important, or talented that you could achieve anything, perhaps even to the point where it caused you to lose touch with reality?
No, I've never felt exceptionally powerful, important, or talented like that. My struggles are really about feeling disorganized and out of control, rather than feeling grand or superior.

Have you ever experienced a distinct period in your life, lasting at least several days, where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt so driven that you were getting much more done than usual?

No, I've never had periods where I felt unusually energetic or didn't need sleep. It's actually been the opposite, where I feel jumbled and out of control rather than highly productive or full of energy.
Have you been feeling consistently sad, hopeless, or uninterested in the things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling consistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in my hobbies. While I am definitely stressed and overwhelmed by my situation, my main issue is feeling confused and out of control with my thoughts and behaviors rather than feeling depressed.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory, or have your family members mentioned that you seem to have trouble focusing, planning, or organizing your daily tasks lately?

Yes, organizing and planning have become major issues for me lately. My wife and son say they can't rely on me for basic things at home, like paying bills on time or keeping simple plans, because I get too mixed up. On top of that, my ability to manage schedules and inventory at work has completely fallen apart, leading to missed orders and me getting written up.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, such as new headaches, seizures, or changes in your gait or coordination, coinciding with these behavioral and organizational difficulties?

No, I haven't had any headaches or seizures, but I've definitely noticed some strange physical behaviors. I'll catch myself pacing in tight circles, flapping my hands, or suddenly freezing in weird positions in the middle of a conversation. It really feels like I'm not in full control of my own body or how I'm acting.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your vision, sense of smell, or any new tremors or stiffness in your limbs that occur when you are not experiencing these episodes of confusion?

No, I haven't noticed any changes in my vision or my sense of smell. I also don't have any tremors or stiffness in my limbs, outside of the strange physical behaviors and freezing episodes I already described.
Have your family members or coworkers noticed a gradual decline in your memory and cognitive abilities over time, or did these behavioral and organizational issues start quite suddenly?

It was definitely a gradual decline that started about a year ago when our new inventory system rolled out and I slowly began to struggle. Over the last six months, though, it has gotten much worse and gone completely off the rails, with my thoughts and actions becoming really jumbled and out of my control.

Besides the difficulties with planning and organization, have you noticed any significant changes in your personality, such as becoming more impulsive, socially inappropriate, or less concerned about the feelings of others compared to how you were before?

Yes, I've definitely noticed that my actions have become inappropriate because I can't seem to control what my body is doing. I'll catch myself pacing in tight circles, flapping my hands, freezing mid-conversation, or even laughing and repeating what people say under my breath. It makes me feel like I no longer have any control over how I behave in front of others.
Have you noticed any subtle changes in your personality, such as becoming more irritable, lacking empathy for others, or acting in ways that are socially inappropriate compared to how you used to be?

Yes, my wife and son say I've become very odd and socially inappropriate compared to my old self, and they can't rely on me anymore. I'll do things like laugh inappropriately or repeat their words under my breath, and I have no control over it. It's really distressing because I want to act normally, but my body just won't cooperate.

Would you say that the changes in your personality—like the impulsivity or lack of social awareness—were the very first signs of your condition, appearing even before you started having trouble with memory and organizing tasks?

No, it was actually the other way around. The trouble with organizing my tasks and keeping up with the new work system started first, about a year ago. The out-of-control behaviors and inappropriate actions only became severe and noticeable later on, about six months ago.

When you look back at that first year, were you having noticeable trouble with your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations or where you placed your belongings, before the organizational issues began?

No, I don't recall having specific memory issues like forgetting conversations or losing my belongings back then. The main trouble has always been feeling mixed up, disorganized, and losing control over my thoughts and actions, rather than actually forgetting things.
Has there been a noticeable decline in your ability to learn new information or recall recent events, or is your primary difficulty specifically with planning, organization, and impulse control?

Yes, my primary struggle is definitely with planning, organization, and controlling my actions, rather than forgetting things. I can still remember information, but I get completely overwhelmed and mixed up when trying to organize schedules, manage inventory, pay bills on time, or control my physical impulses and speech. It's like my brain just can't coordinate the steps to actually carry those things out.

Would you say your ability to understand complex concepts, solve new problems, or use language has also declined significantly alongside these organizational issues, or is your memory and general intellect still mostly intact?

Yes, both my language and my ability to solve complex problems have definitely taken a major hit. When I try to explain simple things, my speech gets so jumbled up and off-track that people think I'm talking nonsense, even though it makes sense to me at the time. I can no longer handle complex tasks like inventory projections or paying bills because I get too mixed up, though my basic memory of who I am is still intact.
Have you or your family noticed any physical changes like a decline in your walking, balance, or fine motor skills alongside these cognitive and behavioral difficulties?

No, I haven't noticed any specific decline in my walking, balance, or fine motor skills. Aside from the pacing and freezing episodes I mentioned earlier, my physical movement and coordination seem okay.
Has there been a noticeable change in your personality or social behavior that is distinct from your difficulty with organizing tasks, such as a loss of empathy or a lack of concern for social norms?

I don't think I've lost empathy or stopped caring about others. I'm not really sure how to answer that, because it feels more like I just can't control my physical actions rather than a real change in my personality.
